title: The Same Mark
description: A plumb-bob hanging inside a square. You have now seen it in two places that have nothing to do with each other.

two_places.title: Two places
two_places.objective: You've seen the mark in two places now. Ask Alder Pyke, the chainman on Granary Row, what it means.
two_places.journal: A plumb-bob inside a square, cut, stamped, or painted. I've seen it twice now, in places with no reason to have anything in common. Probably a maker's mark. Most things are.

asked_the_chainman.title: Ask the man who paints them
asked_the_chainman.objective: Alder Pyke walks lines for whoever pays. Ask what the mark is, and tell him whether you'll keep count.
asked_the_chainman.journal: An old chainman on Granary Row carries a hundred feet of chain over his shoulder and a plumb-bob in his pocket. The mark is stamped on its flat face. He paints these marks, and he's painted a great many.

started_counting.title: Counting them
started_counting.journal: It's a survey mark. Pyke explained it, sounding bored: he drags a chain, walks a line, paints a mark, and gets one and threepence a day. There's nothing to it. I've started writing down where I see them anyway. Couldn't say why.

let_it_alone.title: A maker's mark
let_it_alone.journal: It's a survey mark. Somebody's measuring something, as people with money do before they buy it. No more sinister than a milestone. I asked, got an answer, and let it alone.
